title: How the Internet Works in 60 Seconds 🌐 #shorts
description:
What actually happens when you open a website? Follow one click: DNS turns the name into an IP address, your request is split into packets, routers pass them across the world, a server sends the page back, your browser reassembles it, and HTTPS keeps it all encrypted.

#Internet #HowTheInternetWorks #Networking #DNS #TechExplained #shorts

lines: What actually happens when you open a website?
Let's follow one click, in under a minute.
First, DNS, the internet's phone book, turns the website's name into an IP address: the number computers use to find each other.
Your request is chopped into small packets, each one labelled with where it's going.
The packets hop from router to router, across cables, even under the ocean, each taking the fastest path it can find.
At the other end, a server receives your request, and sends the web page back, also in packets.
Your browser puts the packets back in order, and draws the page on your screen.
And with HTTPS, it's all encrypted, so nobody in between can read it.
All of that, in a fraction of a second.
